# Favorable active menus under a common continuous symmetry

This is a positive theorem for the NEW outward-smoothed singleton-source interface. It maximizes over actual active menus before choosing a physical field. It does not assert that a fixed preselected menu has the same efficiency. It includes arbitrary compatible homothetic simplex fibers with an affine center graph, even when the active base tilt is isolated.

Dependencies are the actual smoothed model and finite clipping in
\`candidate 0fa64553cd01d7ae\`,
the exact menu optimization in
\`candidate 26e4bc3a75ffef69\`,
and the exposed complete-base field in
\`candidate cf5052b52df57b8d\`.
The ordinary centroid Grünbaum inequality is the only numerical continuous theorem used.

## 1. Hypotheses and statement

Let \(P\subset\mathbb Z^n\) be the complete finite sampled base of a convex body and let every sampled fiber \(K_z\subset\mathbb R^d\), \(d\geq1\), have positive volume. Suppose there is an affine map \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^d\) and a finite linear group \(G\subset\operatorname{GL}(d)\) such that
\[
g(K_z-c(z))=K_z-c(z)\quad(z\in P,\ g\in G),
\]
and the common fixed-vector space of \(G\) is zero.

Use the actual positive-width outward-smoothed \(H\) depth, with parameters \(\epsilon,h>0\), and its pooled within-fiber covariance norm \(\Gamma\). Assume the parameters lie in the established proper-source regime. For every actual deepest source there is a balanced finite menu of ACTUAL active caps and a nonnegative globally convex normal-dependent physical field \(\Phi\) such that
\[
\int W\Phi\,d\sigma\ \geq\ \Gamma_d\int\Phi\,d\sigma>0,
\qquad \Gamma_d=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d. \tag{1}
\]
The field can be chosen to isolate one exposed vertex fiber of the COMPLETE base hull. Its target may differ from its source.

For all \(k\) singleton deepest sources, the choices can be combined into one field with every selected profile having efficiency at least \(\Gamma_d/r\), where \(r\leq k\) is the number of distinct target fibers. In particular \(r\leq k(P)\leq2^n\).

## 2. Removing the affine center graph

The affine shear
\[
(z,x)\longmapsto (z,x-c(z))
\]
preserves every integer fiber, its volume, all ambient halfspaces, and the class of allowed convex physical fields. Translation within a fiber preserves its projective energy and its within-fiber covariance. Thus it preserves the actual tied \(H\) model after the corresponding affine coordinate change. We may therefore assume \(c=0\).

Every \(g\in G\) has \(|\det g|=1\), because it has finite order. The induced block map \((z,x)\mapsto(z,gx)\) preserves the mixed measure and the fiber family. Its action preserves projective energy, volume, the tied profile, and pooled covariance:
\[
g\Sigma g^T=\Sigma.
\]
Consequently \(\Gamma(g^{-T}u)=\Gamma(u)\), and the actual smoothed depth is invariant under this group.

The centroid of every \(K_z\) is fixed by every \(g\); hence it is zero. In the proper-source regime the unique maximizing point in each deepest fiber is also group-fixed, so each deepest source is \(Y=(p,0)\). The differentiable own profile is group-invariant. Its continuous gradient at zero is a fixed dual vector, hence zero: averaging the dual representation gives zero because averaging the primal representation does. Thus
\[
\nabla_x f_H(p,0)=0. \tag{2}
\]

## 3. Orbiting ONE actual active cap

Choose any actual active cap at \(Y=(p,0)\), with normal \(N=(a,u)\) and \(\Gamma(u)=1\). Its capture profile is
\[
\Psi\!\left(\frac{a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot x+\epsilon f_H(Y)}h\right).
\]
For every \(g\in G\), the cap with normal
\[
N_g=(a,g^{-T}u)
\]
is also active. All these caps have the SAME base tilt \(a\), identical strip coarea \(S>0\), and identical strip first-margin moment \(A\). This follows by the measure-preserving change of variable \(x\mapsto gx\) in every fiber.

The group average \(|G|^{-1}\sum_g g^{-T}u\) is fixed by the dual group and therefore zero. By (2), the equally weighted orbit is both a balanced quantile menu and a balanced response menu. One may reduce to at most \(d+1\) of its caps by ordinary Carathéodory applied to their continuous normals. Their coareas remain equal, so the same reduced weights serve as response weights.

This construction does not move the base tilt. It therefore does not require a flat family of active base tilts.

## 4. An exposed target shared by all orbit caps

Choose a vertex \(q\) of \(\operatorname{conv}P\) maximizing \(a\cdot z\). Such a vertex belongs to \(P\), is exposed in the finite complete-base hull, and satisfies
\[
a\cdot(q-p)\geq0.
\]
For every orbit cap its margin on the \(q\)-fiber is
\[
a\cdot(q-p)+(g^{-T}u)\cdot x+\epsilon f_H(Y).
\]
The last expression is nonnegative whenever \((g^{-T}u)\cdot x\geq0\). The outward CDF is identically one at nonnegative arguments, so each orbit capture dominates the indicator of a through-centroid halfspace of \(K_q\).

Let \(h_q(n)=h_{K_q}(n)\). Since \(0\) is the interior centroid, \(h_q(n)>0\). The exposed complete-base construction gives a globally finite nonnegative convex physical field \(\Phi_q\) which equals \(h_q(n)\) on the actual normal bundle of \(K_q\) and vanishes on every other measured fiber boundary. Explicitly, choose an affine gap \(r\) with \(r(q)=0\), \(r(z)>0\) for \(z\ne q\), and take
\[
\Phi_q(n,z,x)=[h_q(n)-T r(z)]_+
\]
with one sufficiently large finite \(T\). Convexity in the physical coordinates is immediate.

The cone-volume formula gives
\[
\int\Phi_q\,d\sigma=d|K_q|.
\]
A through-zero plane preserves each ray from zero, and its section through the vertex of each radial cone has no additional flux. Hence, equivalently by polar integration,
\[
\int_{\partial K_q\cap\{v\cdot x\geq0\}}h_q(n)\,dS
=d\,|K_q\cap\{v\cdot x\geq0\}|
\geq \Gamma_d\,d|K_q|.
\]
The last step is ordinary Grünbaum at the centroid. It applies to every orbit direction \(v=g^{-T}u\). Averaging proves (1) exactly, with no loss in \(\epsilon\) or \(h\).

## 5. Simultaneous sources and the actual stationary consequence

Perform the construction independently at every singleton source, giving menus \(W_i\) and exposed targets \(q_i\). For each distinct target normalize the field above to integral one, and sum these \(r\) fields. The resulting \(\Phi\geq0\) has
\[
\int\Phi\,d\sigma=r,\qquad
\int W_i\Phi\,d\sigma\geq\Gamma_d\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
All cross terms are nonnegative. These are ACTUAL independently chosen balanced active menus; hence the same-menu physical response and separator theorem apply.

In the compact proper-source class, the exact tied-buffer response has favorable own-energy, own-volume, and covariance terms, and its remaining correction is bounded by \(C(\epsilon+h)\int\Phi\,d\sigma\). Thus the field gives a strict descent whenever
\[
\beta+C(\epsilon+h)<\Gamma_d/r.
\]
This statement concerns an actual minimum of the unrestricted body problem satisfying the common-symmetry hypothesis. No claim is made that a body minimizing only inside a symmetry-restricted class has the full physical variation inequality.

## 6. Scope and examples

* Common central symmetry suffices, with \(G=\{I,-I\}\). The ordinary centroid fraction is then \(1/2\), which is at least \(\Gamma_d\).
* Every fixed simplex, centered at its centroid, has its full vertex-permutation group as a finite linear symmetry group with no nonzero common fixed vector. Therefore all compatible families \(K_z=c(z)+r_zD\), with \(r_z>0\), affine \(c(z)\), and one fixed simplex \(D\), satisfy the theorem.
* The same statement applies to arbitrary common-group-invariant fiber shapes, not only homothetic ones.
* A nonaffine center graph generally destroys the global block symmetry: transforming a cap independently about each fiber center need not produce an ambient halfspace. No such extension is asserted.
* The bad cyclic fixed-menu triangle-product example is consistent with this theorem. Its poor menu uses different base tilts for the different continuous orbit directions. The orbit of ONE active cap keeps a single tilt and selects a favorable common exposed target.

## 7. The pure-width model needs no H buffer

The theorem and proof apply verbatim to the unbuffered outward model in
\`candidate 6e754f2bf13bdbd1\`.
At positive width the full-normal moment identity in that source gives the unique deepest mark on each source fiber. Group invariance again fixes this mark at zero. The balanced response vectors are simply \(S_Nu\), and the group orbit has constant \(S_N\). The centroid-containing margin argument uses only \(a\cdot(q-p)\geq0\), so setting the buffer to zero loses nothing in (1). The exact pure-width stress then gives descent under \(\beta_h+C h<\Gamma_d/r\), with no energy/profile corrections.
